newsitem.title: INDIA: BUDGET HIGHLIGHTS - India oil exploration proposals.
newsitem.headline: BUDGET HIGHLIGHTS - India oil exploration proposals.

text.p: Following are the highlights of India's oil exploration proposals announced by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram in the annual budget for 1997/98 (April-March) on Friday.
* The Finance Minister, Shri P. Chidambaram, today announced a New Exploration Licencing Policy (NELP) in order to give ONGC & OIL a level playing field viz-a-viz private oil sharing contracts.
* Presenting the General Budget in the Lok Sabha today, the Finance Minister said under the new policy ONGC and OIL will be paid international price of oil for discoveries made under NELP.
* The companies will be given the freedom to market crude oil and gas in the domestic market. Royalty rates would be fixed on an advalorem basis instead of the present system of specific rates.

* The Finance Minister stated, the new policy had been initiated to reduce dependence on imported petroleum products. He added that the country's demand for petroleum products were growing at over 8 per cent per annum currently. Such policy initiatives would encourage Indian and foreign companies to boost exploratory measures as only 6 of the 26 basins that possessed potential for Oil & Natural Gas in the country had been explored so far.
* Under the new policy, royalty payments for exploration in deep waters will be charged at half the rate for offshore areas for the first seven years after commencement of commercial production.

* Companies such as ONGC and OIL will get the same duty concessions on the import of capital goods under the new policy as private production sharing contracts. The Finance Minister in his Budget speech announced that Cess levied under the Oil Industry Development Act, 1974, would be abolished for the new exploration blocks.

* It was also proposed to put a separate petroleum tax code in place to facilitate new investments. In order to encourage production and exploration in the North-East, the Finance Minister said, a tax holiday for seven years after commencement of commercial production for blocks in the region was proposed under the new policy. In order to promote additional capacity in the refinery sector, the Finance Minister announced that refineries would be allowed to import capital goods during the 9th Plan period at concessional duty rates at par with the fertilizer sector.
